pl-l4d42c4-d1e112.summary: Reports that some understand this only of the children for whom they became co-parents; others, born before or after the co-parenthood, they grant may lawfully marry.
claims: Some limit the impediment to the sponsored child.

pl-l4d42c4-d1e115.summary: Cites Urban II, who seems to agree: baptism is valid if in necessity a woman baptizes a child in the Trinity's name, and the sons or daughters of spiritual parents born before or after the co-parenthood may lawfully marry, except that person through whom they became co-parents.
claims: Women may baptize validly in necessity.
Only the sponsored child is impeded.

pl-l4d42c4-d1e121.summary: Cites Paschal II to Bishop Reginus, who forbids those born to the co-father or co-mother after the sponsoring of a son or daughter to marry.
claims: Children born after co-parenthood may not marry.

pl-l4d42c4-d1e130.summary: Cites the Council of Tribur: one who by chance married his spiritual co-mother's daughter may, after mature counsel, keep her and live honestly in lawful marriage.
claims: A chance marriage with a co-mother's daughter may be kept.

pl-l4d42c4.summary: Some apply this only to the children for whom the parents became co-parents, allowing children born before or after the co-parenthood to marry, as Urban II seems to agree, also holding a woman's emergency baptism valid. Paschal II forbids children born after co-parenthood to marry. A council allows one who by chance married his co-mother's daughter to keep her after mature counsel.
claims: Some hold spiritual kinship binds only the sponsored child.
Urban II allows siblings born before or after to marry.
Paschal II forbids children born after co-parenthood to marry.
A chance marriage with a co-mother's daughter may be kept.
